Both memoranda reject an individualized exception to general veterans-benefit law and use a distinctive sequence: acknowledge the hardship, insist on uniformity and equality for similarly situated beneficiaries, state that any legal change should apply to all, warn against heeding special pleas, and conclude by withholding approval. The child reproduces several of C24's formulations nearly verbatim. C02 uses closely related machinery and language, but its overlap is less exact. C11 shares the general objection to piecemeal individual relief but not the distinctive veterans-benefit language.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"if the law is to be changed it should be changed for all. Uniformity and equality of treatment under general law applicable equally to all must be the steadfast rule if the Federal programs for veterans and their dependents are to be operated successfully.","parent_excerpt":"The Federal programs for veterans and their beneficiaries, if they are to be successful, require unswerving uniformity of rule and equality of treatment to all who are similarly situated. If the law is to be changed, it should be changed for all.","explanation":"This is distinctive, substantially identical language expressing the same administrative principle in the same sequence."},{"child_excerpt":"Heeding the special plea of individual cases would obviously destroy the effectiveness of these programs.","parent_excerpt":"We must not, in this benefits field, heed the special plea or the emotional appeal of the hardship case.","explanation":"Both use the distinctive warning against a 'special plea' in an individual veterans-benefit case."},{"child_excerpt":"I cannot agree either that the mandatory provision of the law should be abrogated in this case to the exclusion of other similar cases","parent_excerpt":"I cannot agree that the principles and rules of administration prescribed in the general law should be set aside except in unique and most compelling circumstances of equity.","explanation":"The operative reasoning is structurally parallel: refuse to override general veterans-benefit rules for one claimant absent uniquely compelling circumstances."}]}
